text.p: These are the leading storiesin the Egyptian press on Friday.Reuters has not verified these storiesand does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An Israeli plan to complete Jerusalem's encirclement by settlements and build 220,000 residential units. The Israeli government appropriates $300 million for settlement expansion.
- Egypt informs the U.N. Security Council that Boutros Boutros-Ghali is still Africa's candidate for the post of secretary general.
- Profits will be distributed before the end of December to employees at 557 state firms and joint ventures. The auditing bureau finalised performance evaluation of all companies.
- Three helicopters were sent to rescue 115 labourers at Kom Ombo, some 600 km (375 miles) south of Cairo, after flood waters have surrounded them.

- Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueilly said that subsidies for basic goods would continue. At a meeting with Cairo University teachers and students, Gueilly added bread subsidies cost 2,500 million pounds annually. "Egypt refuses to discuss the issue of subsidies with the International Monetary Fund," he added.
- Suez Canal Authority will announce on Sunday new transit tolls.
